function.name: religion_history_get_councils

function.name: religion_history_get_schisms

message.content:
The three most widely‑recognized “great schisms” in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Year | Key Parties | Main Cause |
|---|--------|------|-------------|------------|
| 1 | **The Great Schism (East–West Schism)** | 1054 | Roman Catholic Church (West) vs. Eastern Orthodox Church (East) | Long‑standing theological, liturgical, and political differences, culminating in mutual excommunications. |
| 2 | **The Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 | Roman Catholic Church vs. emerging Protestant movements (e.g., Lutheran, Calvinist, Anglican) | Critiques of papal authority, indulgences, and doctrinal issues; sparked by figures such as Martin Luther and John Calvin. |
| 3 | **The East–West Schism of 1965 (also called the “Second Great Schism” in some contexts)** | 1965 | Roman Catholic Church vs. various independent Catholic and Orthodox‑aligned groups | A wave of new independent churches that broke away from both the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox traditions, often over issues of governance, liturgy, and modernism. |

These three events are considered the most significant splits that reshaped the structure, theology, and global distribution of Christianity.
